question: How does BSP scale CET across the Northeast?
html:
BSP scales CET with a phased buy-and-build modelled on Smith + Howard. The steps are to integrate Massachusetts and Connecticut around Horton, add founder-owned firms in RI, NH, ME and VT, then shift the mix toward recurring service contracts. The target is roughly 3x revenue in 36 months (est.) (CET growth plan).

Phase 1: one MA–CT company

  • Horton is the first adjacent-state add-on. It nearly doubles the workforce and brings Connecticut wastewater relationships (CET growth plan).
  • Horton targets 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects across CT, MA and RI, led by New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk (CET growth plan).
  • The radar shows the deepest pipeline in CT (27 items) and MA (25). It shows less in ME (16), VT (9), NH (5) and RI (4) (CET opportunity radar).
  • Anchor programs include Fairfield pump stations and WPCF (~$36.1M) and Danbury electrical resiliency (~$3.2M) (CET opportunity radar).

Phase 2: adjacent-state add-ons

  • CET's existing six-state licensing supports founder-owned deals from a 48-company screen with a ~$15.1M median revenue. The aim is to move before Pfingsten's NEC Group or Ridgemont's Crete United (CET growth plan).
  • The top-ranked targets skew to Massachusetts. McDonald Electrical (fit score 83, ~$18.4M est. revenue) already owns ANJ Electric, an RI/CT union contractor, which gives a possible RI bridge (CET add-on targets).
  • Target revenue is ZoomInfo-modelled and needs diligence (CET add-on targets).

Phase 3: recurring service mix

  • The recurring lines are SCADA and pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency work. Advisers price this mix 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).
  • Data-center electrical is thin in New England, where ISO-NE says data-center growth has lagged other regions (CET growth plan).

KPI roadmap (all est.)

MonthRevenueEBITDAHeadcountLocations
0$80M$8.0M2754
12$115M$12.1M3907
24$170M$19.5M56010
36$240M$30.0M78013

These figures are labelled assumptions, not guidance. The baselines are low-confidence estimates from public filings (CET growth plan).

Gaps and caveats

  • Construction demand by state: September residential permits ran MA 1,515, ME 587, NH 459, CT 408, RI 166 and VT 152 units (Census building permits). This is a weak proxy for CET's infrastructure work.
  • Massachusetts project list: the MassDEP CWSRF list was not itemized. The 2026 IUP covers 76 projects worth about $1.02B (CET opportunity radar).
  • Bid outcomes: most radar bids were due in October. Win/loss results from Oct 8, 2026 onward are not in the context.

Next actions

  1. Bid the MassWildlife Roger Reed Hatchery generators and ATS (due Nov 25, 2026). Log outcomes on the October bids.
  2. Book engineer-of-record meetings for the Fairfield, South Windsor, West Haven and Danbury pump-station programs.
  3. Open diligence on McDonald Electrical and K.M. Kelly. Replace ZoomInfo revenue estimates with reported financials.
  4. Pull the MassDEP 2026 IUP Tables 3–4 by hand to itemize the Massachusetts wastewater pipeline.
